error_codes.customer_message: Error 0 means no fault was detected on the charger. Please try unplugging and plugging in your vehicle again to start a new session.
Error 1 means the charger ended the session unexpectedly. Please unplug, wait 30 seconds, and try starting a new charging session. If it happens again, please contact support.

Error 2 means your vehicle sent a signal to stop the charging session. This can happen if your vehicle's battery management system detected an issue. Please try unplugging and starting a new session. If the error repeats, please contact support.

Error 10 means the charger could not lock the cable connector properly. Please unplug the cable fully and reinsert it firmly. If the error appears again, please contact support as the connector may need inspection.

Error 11 means the charger stopped because it got too hot. Please leave the charger to rest for at least 15 minutes to allow it to cool down, then try again. If this error keeps occurring, please contact support as the cooling system may need to be checked.

Error 12 means the charger and your vehicle could not complete their startup handshake in time. Please unplug, make sure your vehicle is switched off and key is removed, wait 30 seconds, and try again. If it persists, please contact support.
Error 13 means there was a timeout while the charger was reading your vehicle's battery settings. Please unplug, wait 30 seconds, and try again. If the error repeats, please contact support.

error_codes.meaning: Vehicle not ready to charge timeout
error_codes.customer_message: Error 14 means your vehicle did not signal that it was ready to charge in time. Please unplug, ensure the vehicle is switched off with the key removed, wait 30 seconds, and try again. Contact support if the issue continues.

Error 15 means the communication between the charger and your vehicle was interrupted during the charging session. Please unplug, wait 30 seconds, and start a new session. Contact support if it keeps happening.
Error 16 means your vehicle stopped sending charge requests to the charger during the session. Please unplug, wait 30 seconds, and try again. If this error repeats, please contact support.

error_codes.meaning: Vehicle sent a stop signal during charging
error_codes.customer_message: Error 17 means your vehicle's battery management system sent a stop signal during the session. Please unplug, wait 30 seconds, and try again. If the error continues, please contact support.

Error 19 indicates an internal hardware fault on the charger. Please do not attempt to restart it yourself. Our support team will need to reboot the charger remotely. Please contact support immediately with your Charger ID.

error_codes.meaning: Retired error code — no longer in use
error_codes.customer_message: Error 22 is a retired code that is no longer in use on current charger firmware. Please contact support with your Charger ID so our team can investigate what triggered this on your unit.
Error 23 means the charger is detecting that the cable is not properly seated. Please unplug fully and reinsert the charging cable firmly into the vehicle, making sure it clicks into place.
Error 26 means the charger did not receive a start confirmation in time. Please unplug, wait 30 seconds, and try starting a new session. If it fails again, please contact support.

error_codes.meaning: Charger has no output or insufficient power output
error_codes.customer_message: Error 31 means the charger is unable to deliver power. This may indicate a hardware issue with the unit. Please contact support with your Charger ID so we can investigate.
Error 64 means the charger detected a mismatch with your vehicle's battery settings. Please contact support with your vehicle VIN and Charger ID so we can investigate the compatibility.
Error 74 means the charger's side panel door is not properly closed. Please check that both side doors of the charging unit are securely shut, then try again.

error_codes.meaning: Retired error code — no longer in use
error_codes.customer_message: Error 75 is a retired code that is no longer in use on current charger firmware. Please contact support with your Charger ID so our team can investigate what triggered this on your unit.

Error 76 means the charger detected an insulation issue. Please unplug and try again. If the error appears a second time, please stop using this charger and contact support immediately with your Charger ID as this may be a safety-related fault.

error_codes.meaning: Vehicle detected connected before session started
error_codes.customer_message: Error 84 means the charger detected your vehicle was already connected when it started up. Please fully unplug the cable, wait 30 seconds, then plug it back in to start a fresh session.

Error 85 means the charger detected an abnormal current or voltage level. Please stop using this charger immediately and contact support with your Charger ID. Do not attempt to restart until our team has investigated.
Error 86 means the charger detected a lower than expected voltage. Please contact support with your Charger ID so our team can investigate the power supply to this unit.

error_codes.meaning: Vehicle reported a battery management fault
error_codes.customer_message: Error 150 means your vehicle's battery management system reported a fault to the charger. Please unplug and check your vehicle's dashboard for any warning lights. If your vehicle appears fine, try again. If the error repeats, please contact support with your vehicle VIN.

Error 151 means the charger and your vehicle could not complete the initial connection check in time. Please unplug, make sure your vehicle is switched off with the key removed, wait 30 seconds, and try again.
Error 152 means your vehicle did not respond to the charger's connection check in time. Please unplug, wait 30 seconds, and try again. If the error continues, please contact support.

error_codes.meaning: Vehicle not ready — relay not closed
error_codes.customer_message: Error 153 means your vehicle's internal charging relay did not close as expected. Please unplug, make sure your vehicle is switched off with the key fully removed, wait 30 seconds, and try again.

error_codes.meaning: Vehicle charge request lost during session
error_codes.customer_message: Error 154 means your vehicle stopped sending charge requests during an active session. Please unplug, wait 30 seconds, and start a new session. Contact support if this keeps happening.

error_codes.meaning: Vehicle charging status lost during session
error_codes.customer_message: Error 155 means the charger lost track of your vehicle's battery status during the session. Please unplug, wait 30 seconds, and try again. Contact support if the issue continues.

error_codes.meaning: Lost communication with vehicle battery management system
error_codes.customer_message: Error 156 means the charger lost communication with your vehicle's battery management system. Please unplug, make sure your vehicle is completely switched off and the key is removed, wait 60 seconds, and try again. If the error appears again, please contact support with your Charger ID and vehicle VIN.

Error 157 means your vehicle reported a fault to the charger. Please check your vehicle's dashboard for any warning lights or error messages. If your vehicle appears to have a fault, please contact your fleet manager or vehicle service team. If the vehicle seems fine, please contact our support team with your vehicle VIN.

Error 158 means there is a discrepancy between the voltage your vehicle reported and what the charger measured. Please contact support with your Charger ID and vehicle VIN so our team can investigate.
Error 159 indicates a fault with the charging unit itself. Please contact support immediately with your Charger ID. Do not attempt to use this charger until our team has inspected it.

error_codes.meaning: Internal communication failure between charger components
error_codes.customer_message: Error 2048 means the internal components of the charger lost communication with each other. Please contact support with your Charger ID. Our team will need to remotely restart the unit. If after restarting the charger you do not hear the sound of the self-inspection (three click sounds from the unit), please let support know immediately.

faqs.question: How do I start a charging session?
faqs.answer:
There are two ways to start a charging session depending on your charger setup:

Method 1 – Plug and Charge: Simply plug the charging cable into your vehicle and the session will start automatically.

Method 2 – VIN Start: Plug in the cable and wait for a red tick to appear on the charger screen. Once the red tick appears, tap *PnC or VIN* on the screen to start the session.

faqs.question: What is the red tick on the charger screen?
faqs.answer: The red tick on the charger screen means the charger has detected your vehicle and is ready to start a session. Once you see the red tick, tap *PnC or VIN* on the screen to begin charging.

faqs.question: How do I find PnC or VIN on the charger screen?
faqs.answer: After plugging in and seeing the red tick, tap *PnC or VIN* on the charger screen to start the session. If neither option appears, please contact support as your vehicle may not yet be registered on the system.

faqs.question: The red tick is not appearing on the screen, what should I do?
faqs.answer: If the red tick does not appear after plugging in, try the following: Make sure the charging cable is firmly plugged into the vehicle. Ensure your vehicle is switched off and the key is removed from the ignition. Wait up to 60 seconds as some vehicles take time to communicate with the charger. If the red tick still does not appear, please select option 1 from the AE support menu for further assistance.

faqs.question: My vehicle is registered for plug and charge but the session is not starting automatically
faqs.answer: First make sure the charging cable is firmly plugged into the vehicle, and that your vehicle is switched off with the key removed. Some vehicles take up to 60 seconds to initiate plug and charge automatically. If the session still does not start, try the VIN start method as an alternative — plug in, wait for the red tick, and tap *PnC or VIN* on the screen. If neither method works, please select option 1 from the AE support menu.

faqs.question: How do I stop a charging session?
faqs.answer: To stop a charging session, tap the charger screen twice to wake it up, then tap the Stop button that appears on the screen. Once the session has stopped, you can safely unplug the cable from your vehicle.

faqs.question: Can I just unplug the cable to stop charging?
faqs.answer: It is recommended to always stop the session on the charger screen before unplugging. Tap the screen twice to wake it, then tap the Stop button, then unplug. Unplugging without stopping the session first may cause errors on the charger.

faqs.question: The stop button is not responding on the screen, what do I do?
faqs.answer: Try tapping the screen twice again to wake it up, then look for the Stop button. If the screen is unresponsive, please contact support and we will stop the session remotely. Do not forcefully unplug the cable. Please have your Charger ID ready when you contact us.

faqs.question: The session is still showing as active after I stopped it, is that normal?
faqs.answer: It can take up to 2 minutes for the charger to fully close the session after you press stop. If the session still shows as active after 5 minutes, please contact support with your Charger ID and vehicle VIN so we can investigate.

faqs.question: How long should it take to charge my vehicle?
faqs.answer: Charge time depends on your vehicle's battery capacity, current state of charge, and the type of charger at your site. Your fleet manager or Aeversa account team can advise on the expected charge times for your specific vehicle models and charger configuration.

faqs.question: My vehicle is charging slower than usual, what could cause this?
faqs.answer: Several factors can affect charging speed: extreme heat or cold can cause the vehicle's battery management system to reduce charging speed automatically; if the battery is already close to full, charging naturally slows down; peak load periods at the depot may affect available power. If the speed seems unusually low, please select option 3 from the AE support menu.

faqs.question: Can multiple vehicles charge at the same time?
faqs.answer: Yes, multiple vehicles can charge simultaneously at your depot, subject to the number of available charge points and your site's power capacity. Your Aeversa account team will have configured your site to manage load accordingly.

faqs.question: What does kWh mean and why does it matter for our fleet?
faqs.answer: kWh stands for kilowatt-hour and is the unit used to measure energy delivered to your vehicle during a charging session. For fleet management, tracking kWh per vehicle helps monitor energy consumption, calculate charging costs, and identify vehicles that may have battery performance issues.

faqs.question: How do I know which charger to use at my depot?
faqs.answer: Each charger at your depot has a unique Charger ID displayed on a sticker on the unit. Your fleet manager will advise on the correct charger allocation per vehicle. When contacting support, always have the Charger ID ready as it helps us identify and resolve issues faster.

faqs.question: Where do I find the Charger ID?
faqs.answer: The Charger ID sticker is located on the front of the charger unit, underneath the screen. The charger type may look different depending on your site, but the sticker location is the same. Please have this ready whenever you contact support as it helps us locate and diagnose your specific charger quickly.

faqs.question: The charger screen is blank or off, what should I do?
faqs.answer: Please select option 2 from the AE support menu and AE will guide you through checking whether this is a power issue at the site or a fault with the specific unit.

faqs.question: The cable is stuck and I cannot unplug it, what should I do?
faqs.answer: Do not force the cable out. First make sure the charging session has been fully stopped on the charger screen by tapping twice then pressing Stop. Some vehicles lock the cable during an active session. If the session is stopped and the cable is still stuck, please contact support immediately and do not attempt to force the connector out as this may damage your vehicle or the charger.

faqs.question: There is an error message on the charger screen, what does it mean?
faqs.answer: Please type the error code number you see on the screen and I will explain what it means and what to do next.

faqs.question: How do I report a vehicle that is consistently not charging properly?
faqs.answer: Please contact support via the AE menu or email support@aeversa.co.za with the vehicle's VIN, the Charger ID it typically uses, and a description of the issue. Our team will investigate whether the fault is with the charger or the vehicle's charging port.

faqs.question: Can I get a report of charging sessions per vehicle?
faqs.answer: Yes, charging session reports per vehicle are available through your Aeversa fleet management account. Please speak to your Aeversa account manager or email support@aeversa.co.za for assistance accessing your reports.

faqs.question: A new vehicle has been added to our fleet, how do we register it on the system?
faqs.answer: New vehicles need to be registered on the Aeversa system before they can charge using the VIN start method. Please email support@aeversa.co.za with the vehicle's VIN, make, and model and we will get it added for you.

faqs.question: A vehicle has been removed from our fleet, how do we deregister it?
faqs.answer: Please email support@aeversa.co.za with the vehicle's VIN and confirm that it should be removed from your fleet account. We will deactivate it from the system promptly.
